name: Dither sequence
shows: Two to six real photographs that belong together printed with an ordered dither in the page palette and played like a slow loop of film. Each cut is a dithered wipe on a slight diagonal with a one-cell accent line on its leading edge; a small pill counts the frames (or shows the captions given) on a segmented timeline.
for: In the kit's gallery only, never on a page (references/effects-objects.md): no page prints, dithers or grades a photograph. What it was made for: two to six real photographs that belong together (a device from several sides, the stages of what the software makes, a game's scenes), never a random set.
never: Never on a place, service, product or local-business page (a cafe, a shop, a hotel, a studio people visit, a maker of things): those show their photographs plain, never dithered. Never mood pictures that only fill the frame. No caption that explains the effect; the photographs' credits go in the footer's one credit line.
motion: Each frame holds 2.2 s (nothing is drawn while it holds), then wipes to the next over 1.5 s at up to 30 frames a second. With autoplay 0 it holds the first frame until hovered (auto.js lets one sequence per group move).
hover: The pointer scrubs the timeline: each frame holds for most of its stretch and wipes to the next near its end. Touch: drag.
reducedMotion: The first frame, still, no pause disc; the pointer still picks a frame.

params.cell: CSS px per dither cell; default from the panel size, 2 to 3
params.captions: an array, one per frame (otherwise the pill counts 01 / 04)
params.focus: an array of [x, y] cover-crop centres, one per frame (default each entry's focus)
params.fit: 'cover' (default) or 'contain': the whole photograph on the page's paper, for mixed shapes
params.drift: 1 lets each frame drift slowly, like a held camera (off by default: it redraws every frame)

palette: four print tones from bg to ink; on a dark page light prints as ink, capped short of solid so a bright photograph is never a white slab; accent for the wipe line; the pill takes bg and ink.
fallback: the first photograph that loaded, as an , cover-cropped; a photograph that fails is left out of the loop.
cost: low: two textures at the dither-cell resolution, drawn only during a wipe or a scrub
